note: TESTREG's and TWINREG's Unika rows each name two candidate variables and an edition both carry, so each is an ambiguous_support_target error; a third row leaves its Registernamn blank (and its column), an unknown_support_key error. The slice routes each ref by ref. Only a row whose register name matches exactly one delivered register can be placed out of the slice: TESTREG's row becomes the one deferred_out_of_slice_reference warning, the allowed twin (scope-support-errors-keep-their-source-event shows it alone). The blank-name row (the old 'unknown') and TWINREG, delivered twice (the old 'ambiguous'), have no one register to be out of, so each stays an error, although the slice selects neither. The old 'unobserved' arm (an undelivered register's blank-column row) has no error form any more: a row complete but for its column name is one source-wide unknown_support_key warning (#1589), and an undelivered register's row with a column is an unreferenced_support_record warning. The old test selected nothing; here the slice selects register 2, whose own row is supported. Refs are semantic hashes, so the case counts them per code and ties them to the source issues' refs.
fails_if: `scope_support_diagnostics` places a ref whose register name matches several delivered registers in one of them (`next(iter(possibilities)) if possibilities else None`), or defers a ref it cannot place (`context is None`) as out of slice, so TWINREG's row, or both unplaced rows, become deferred_out_of_slice_reference warnings

sources.description: Register 2 (OTHERREG) is the slice and has a summary row for its OTHER column. TESTREG (register 1) is delivered once, with two variables (101, 102) under one literal key; TWINREG is delivered twice, as registers 3 and 4, with one TwinVar TWIN each. The TESTREG and TWINREG Unika rows name the 2020 edition every candidate carries, so neither supports a column; one more row leaves both its Registernamn and its column blank.
